To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
managerialism has been introduced in a way that has not displaced bureaucratic rationality, and that the latter has not been displaced in a way that precludes the former.

1) the managerialist model of the public sector has not been implemented to the extent claimed by its proponents; 2) the managerialist approach to public administration has not been adopted in place of the legal-bureaucratic model; and 3) both the managerialist and legal-bureaucrat models of public administration have been adopted in the immigration area.
managerialist reforms have not been accompanied by a decline in legal bureaucratic rationality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how managerialism has been implemented and how it has affected the policy-making and decision-making processes of the Department.

the relationship between political, managerial and legal bureaucratic rationality, and how these forms of rationality are combined to influence the development, implementation and evaluation of policy.

the ways in which the Department's managerialist and bureaucratic forms have developed in relation to each other and the implications of these developments for the Department's clients, staff and the political system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Department of Immigration has not been transformed into a managerialist organisation, but rather has become more bureaucratic and legal in its decision-making.
the managerialist model is not the sole model of management in public bureaucracies.
managerialist and legal-bureaucratic forms have both been expanded in the Department of immigration and Ethnic Affairs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

managerialism and legal rationality are not mutually exclusive and that the managerialism thesis needs to be modified to account for the role of legal bureaucratic rationality in the policy-making process.
the Department of Immigration is not an example of the new public management, but of the persistence of the old public management.
managerialism is a process of rationalization that is not necessarily a process of rationality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the public sector is a hybrid of bureaucratic and market-oriented practices, which are shaped by the interplay of political, managerialist and legal rationalities.
managerialism has been used to justify a more extensive role for the state in the management of the economy.
managerialist reforms have not led to a market-oriented public service.
